minutes.headline: Board found both dogs dangerous and set fence, muzzle and insurance rules; state delegation gave a Turkey Hill asbestos check.
minutes.summary: The Select Board accepted a state earmark check from the legislative delegation for asbestos removal at Turkey Hill, held a dangerous dog hearing, and appointed a cemetery commissioner. It deferred approval of a solar PILOT until town counsel finishes review, renewed one earth removal permit and continued another, and discussed the late capital plan presentation. A member urged the town manager to prepare budgets at two different tax increase levels.

what_happened.line: The Select Board held a dangerous dog hearing and found both dogs dangerous; the vote was not audible in the recording.
The board set four restrictions: confinement or fence, muzzle off premises, and proof of insurance, amended to 90 days from that evening.
The board deferred review of a solar payment-in-lieu-of-taxes agreement until the first meeting after town counsel approves it.
The legislative delegation presented a state earmark check for asbestos removal at Turkey Hill.
The board appointed a cemetery commissioner unanimously, renewed earth removal permit 15, and continued permit 14; those two votes were not audible.

why_it_matters: The solar payment agreement would set a stream of payments to the town over about 20 years, and the board is holding it until town counsel finishes review.
The state earmark pays for asbestos removal at Turkey Hill, a cost that would otherwise fall on the town budget, mostly taxes.
The capital plan came late to the board, and its timing affects when residents see the spending proposals that go to Town Meeting.
watch_next: The first meeting after town counsel approves the solar payment agreement, when the board will take it up.
The first February meeting, where the capital plan presentation is on the agenda.

Our votes show no results, and the official also differs on the dog restrictions.
